title: Workers propose Tk 32,000 garment minimum wage at wage board
excerpt: Owners have four working days to reply. The proposal is more than two and a half times the current Tk 12,500 wage.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: an empty government meeting room in Dhaka with folders and wage documents on a long table

content:
Workers’ representatives on the Minimum Wages Board have proposed raising the minimum monthly wage for garment workers from Tk 12,500 to Tk 32,000. They presented the figure at the board’s second meeting at its Segunbagicha office in Dhaka on Monday, 9 November, The Business Standard and The Daily Star reported.

Factory owners did not table a counter-proposal. The board gave them four working days to do so.

What the workers proposed

  • A minimum of Tk 32,000 a month for the lowest grade and Tk 48,000 for the highest, according to both newspapers.
  • The Daily Star reported the full scale: Tk 32,000 for grade 4, Tk 38,000 for grade 3, Tk 43,000 for grade 2 and Tk 48,000 for grade 1, with Tk 30,000 for apprentices.
  • Workers’ representative Babul Akter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Industrial Workers Federation, said a family of four needs Tk 45,000 to Tk 60,000 a month for essentials, The Daily Star reported.

The proposal is Tk 2,000 above the Tk 30,000 that protesting workers have demanded. Other workers’ organisations submitted separate proposals, The Daily Star reported.

Where owners stand

ABM Shamsuddin, a director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) who represents owners on the board, said owners would submit their figure within the deadline and that the new structure would take effect in December either way. Board chairman Syed Azad Subhani said the board would decide without the owners’ proposal if they missed the deadline. He said owners had first asked for seven working days.

The board also agreed to visit factories in the main industrial areas before its next meeting, The Daily Star reported. The case for the amount, the grades and job classifications are due to be discussed next week.

The wage history

Why it matters

The sector employs about 4 million people, according to the board chairman. Protests over pay have run for more than a week and closed hundreds of factories, The Daily Star reported, and Border Guard Bangladesh has 34 platoons in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj industrial areas. The gap between the two sides’ figures will shape whether unrest returns. Organisations running livelihood, health or rights programmes with garment workers should plan for further disruption in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur until a figure is agreed.

What to watch

  • The owners’ counter-proposal, due within four working days of the 9 November meeting.
  • The board’s factory visits and its next meeting.
  • Whether the final figure is announced before December, when the board says the new scale will apply.
